sanskrit: na cainān anvabudhyanta manujā manujottama evaṃ pravṛttān daityāṃs tāṃs tāpaseṣu tapasviṣu
english: And men, O best of men, did not perceive those demons acting thus against the ascetics engaged in their austerities.

sanskrit: prabhāte samadṛśyanta niyatāhārakarśitāḥ mahītalasthā munayaḥ śarīrair gatajīvitaiḥ
english: At dawn the sages were seen lying on the ground, their bodies emaciated by regulated diet, lifeless, their vital breath departed from their frames.

sanskrit: kṣīṇamāṃsair virudhirair vimajjāntrair visaṃdhibhiḥ ākīrṇair ācitā bhūmiḥ śaṅkhānām iva rāśibhiḥ
english: The earth was strewn and heaped with their flesh-wasted, bloodless, marrow-drained, jointless bodies, like piles of conch shells scattered about.

sanskrit: kalaśair vipraviddhaiś ca sruvair bhagnais tathaiva ca vikīrṇair agnihotraiś ca bhūr babhūva samāvṛtā
english: The ground was covered with overturned water pots, broken ladles, and scattered sacred fire-vessels strewn all around.

sanskrit: niḥsvādhyāyavaṣaṭkāraṃ naṣṭayajñotsavakriyam jagad āsīn nirutsāhaṃ kāleyabhayapīḍitam
english: The world, tormented by fear of the Kāleyas, was without Vedic recitation or the vaṣaṭ-call, deprived of sacrifice and festive rites, and utterly devoid of all enthusiasm.

sanskrit: evaṃ prakṣīyamāṇāś ca mānavā manujeśvara ātmatrāṇaparā bhītāḥ prādravanta diśo bhayāt
english: And so, being thus destroyed, O lord of men, humans — intent only on self-preservation and overcome by fear — fled in all directions out of terror.

sanskrit: ke cid guhāḥ praviviśur nirjharāṃś cāpare śritāḥ apare maraṇodvignā bhayāt prānān samutsṛjan
english: Some entered into caves; others took shelter near waterfalls; and yet others, consumed by dread of death, gave up their very lives out of fear.

sanskrit: ke cid atra maheṣvāsāḥ śūrāḥ paramadarpitāḥ mārgamāṇāḥ paraṃ yatnaṃ dānavānāṃ pracakrire
english: Some great archers there, O hero, proud and valiant warriors, making every effort in their search, set about hunting down the demons.

sanskrit: na caitān adhijagmus te samudraṃ samupāśritān śramaṃ jagmuś ca paramam ājagmuḥ kṣayam eva ca
english: Yet they could not find those demons who had taken refuge in the ocean; they suffered great fatigue and in the end met with destruction.

sanskrit: jagaty upaśamaṃ yāte naṣṭayajñotsavakriye ājagmuḥ paramām ārtiṃ tridaśā manujeśvara
english: When the world had fallen into this state of desolation, stripped of sacrifice and festive rites, the gods too fell into the greatest distress, O lord of men.

sanskrit: sametya samahendrāś ca bhayān mantraṃ pracakrire nārāyaṇaṃ puraskṛtya vaikuṇṭham aparājitam
english: The gods assembled together and, prompted by fear, took counsel, placing Nārāyaṇa — the invincible lord of Vaikuṇṭha — at their head.

sanskrit: tato devāḥ sametās te tadocur madhusūdanam tvaṃ naḥ sraṣṭā ca pātā ca bhartā ca jagataḥ prabho tvayā sṛṣṭam idaṃ sarvaṃ yac ceṅgaṃ yac ca neṅgati
english: Then all the assembled gods spoke to Madhusūdana: "You are the creator, protector, and sustainer of the universe, O lord. All this world — both what moves and what does not move — has been created by you."

sanskrit: tvayā bhūmiḥ purā naṣṭā samudrāt puṣkarekṣaṇa vārāhaṃ rūpam āsthāya jagadarthe samuddhṛtā
english: "When the earth was lost and sunk beneath the ocean, O lotus-eyed one, you assumed the form of a boar and lifted her up for the sake of the world."

sanskrit: ādidaityo mahāvīryo hiraṇyakaśipus tvayā nārasiṃhaṃ vapuḥ kṛtvā sūditaḥ puruṣottama
english: "The primordial demon Hiraṇyakaśipu, of mighty valor, was slain by you, O best of beings, after you took the form of the man-lion."

sanskrit: avadhyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ baliś cāpi mahāsuraḥ vāmanaṃ vapur āśritya trailokyād bhraṃśitas tvayā
english: "And Bali, that great demon invincible to all creatures, was cast out from the three worlds by you after you assumed the form of a dwarf."

sanskrit: asuraś ca maheṣvāso jambha ity abhiviśrutaḥ yajñakṣobhakaraḥ krūras tvayaiva vinipātitaḥ
english: "And the demon renowned as Jambha, a great wielder of the bow who cruelly disturbed the sacrifices, was likewise struck down by you alone."

sanskrit: evamādīni karmāṇi yeṣāṃ saṃkhyā na vidyate asmākaṃ bhayabhītānāṃ tvaṃ gatir madhusūdana
english: "Such deeds as these are innumerable; no count of them is possible. You are the refuge of us who are seized with fear, O Madhusūdana."

sanskrit: tasmāt tvāṃ deva deveśa lokārthaṃ jñāpayāmahe rakṣa lokāṃś ca devāṃś ca śakraṃ ca mahato bhayāt
english: "Therefore, O God, lord of gods, we bring this matter before you for the sake of the world. Protect the worlds, the gods, and Indra from this great danger."

sanskrit: devā ūcuḥ itaḥ pradānād vartante prajāḥ sarvāś caturvidhāḥ tā bhāvitā bhāvayanti havyakavyair divaukasaḥ
english: The gods said: "From the offerings made here all four kinds of creatures sustain themselves; those creatures, thus nourished, in turn nourish the celestial beings with oblations of havis and kavya."

sanskrit: lokā hy evaṃ vartayanti anyonyaṃ samupāśritāḥ tvatprasādān nirudvignās tvayaiva parirakṣitāḥ
english: "The worlds thus sustain one another in mutual dependence; by your grace they dwell free from anxiety, protected by you alone."

sanskrit: idaṃ ca samanuprāptaṃ lokānāṃ bhayam uttamam na ca jānīma keneme rātrau vadhyanti brāhmaṇāḥ
english: "Now this great danger has come upon the worlds, and we do not know by whom these brahmins are being slain in the night."

sanskrit: kṣīṇeṣu ca brāhmaṇeṣu pṛthivī kṣayam eṣyati tataḥ pṛthivyāṃ kṣīṇāyāṃ tridivaṃ kṣayam eṣyati
english: "When the brahmins are destroyed, the earth will perish; and when the earth perishes, the celestial realm of the three heavens will also perish."

sanskrit: tvatprasādān mahābāho lokāḥ sarve jagatpate vināśaṃ nādhigaccheyus tvayā vai parirakṣitāḥ
english: "By your grace, O mighty-armed lord of the world, all the worlds, protected by you, need not come to destruction."

sanskrit: viṣṇur uvāca viditaṃ me surāḥ sarvaṃ prajānāṃ kṣayakāraṇam bhavatāṃ cāpi vakṣyāmi śṛṇudhvaṃ vigatajvarāḥ
english: Viṣṇu said: "O gods, I know fully the cause of the destruction of creatures. I shall tell you too — hear me with your anxieties laid aside."

sanskrit: kāleya iti vikhyāto gaṇaḥ paramadāruṇaḥ taiś ca vṛtraṃ samāśritya jagat sarvaṃ prabādhitam
english: "The horde known as the Kāleyas is exceedingly terrible; sheltering behind Vṛtra, they have afflicted the entire world."

sanskrit: te vṛtraṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā sahasrākṣeṇa dhīmatā jīvitaṃ parirakṣantaḥ praviṣṭā varuṇālayam
english: "Seeing Vṛtra slain by the wise thousand-eyed Indra, and wishing to preserve their own lives, they entered the abode of Varuṇa — the ocean."

sanskrit: te praviśyodadhiṃ ghoraṃ nakragrāhasamākulam utsādanārthaṃ lokānāṃ rātrau ghnanti munīn iha
english: "Having entered that terrible ocean teeming with crocodiles and sea-monsters, they come out at night and slay the sages here in order to destroy the worlds."

sanskrit: na tu śakyāḥ kṣayaṃ netuṃ samudrāśrayagā hi te samudrasya kṣaye buddhir bhavadbhiḥ saṃpradhāryatām agastyena vinā ko hi śakto 'nyo 'rṇavaśoṣaṇe
english: "But they cannot be brought to destruction, for they take refuge in the ocean. Your counsel must now be directed toward the drying up of the ocean — for who other than Agastya is capable of draining the sea?"

sanskrit: etac chrutvā vaco devā viṣṇunā samudāhṛtam parameṣṭhinam ājñāpya agastyasyāśramaṃ yayuḥ
english: Having heard these words thus spoken by Viṣṇu, the gods took leave of Brahmā, the supreme lord, and set out for the hermitage of Agastya.

sanskrit: tatrāpaśyan mahātmānaṃ vāruṇiṃ dīptatejasam upāsyamānam ṛṣibhir devair iva pitāmaham
english: There they beheld the great-souled son of Varuṇa, blazing with radiance, attended upon by sages as the Grandsire himself is attended upon by the gods.

sanskrit: te 'bhigamya mahātmānaṃ maitrāvaruṇim acyutam āśramasthaṃ taporāśiṃ karmabhiḥ svair abhiṣṭuvan
english: Approaching that great-souled and steadfast son of Mitra and Varuṇa — that mass of ascetic power dwelling in his hermitage — they praised him with their own hymns of devotion.

sanskrit: devā ūcuḥ nahuṣeṇābhitaptānāṃ tvaṃ lokānāṃ gatiḥ purā bhraṃśitaś ca suraiśvaryāl lokārthaṃ lokakaṇṭakaḥ
english: The gods said: "You were formerly the refuge of the worlds when they were tormented by Nahuṣa, and you cast down that thorn of the worlds from his lordship over the gods, for the good of all."

sanskrit: krodhāt pravṛddhaḥ sahasā bhāskarasya nagottamaḥ vacas tavānatikrāman vindhyaḥ śailo na vardhate
english: "The great mountain Vindhya, which in anger suddenly began to grow — blocking the path of the sun — no longer grows, not transgressing your word."

sanskrit: tamasā cāvṛte loke mṛtyunābhyarditāḥ prajāḥ tvām eva nātham āsādya nirvṛtiṃ paramāṃ gatāḥ
english: "When the world was enveloped in darkness and creatures were oppressed by death, they attained the highest peace by finding you as their lord."

sanskrit: asmākaṃ bhayabhītānāṃ nityaśo bhagavān gatiḥ tatas tv ārtāḥ prayācāmas tvāṃ varaṃ varado hy asi
english: "O blessed one, you are always the refuge of us who are seized with fear. Therefore, afflicted as we are, we beg a boon of you — for you are indeed a giver of boons."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kimarthaṃ sahasā vindhyaḥ pravṛddhaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ vistareṇa mahāmune
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "Why did the Vindhya mountain suddenly grow, seized with rage? I wish to hear this in full, O great sage."

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca adrirājaṃ mahāśailaṃ maruṃ kanakaparvatam udayāstamaye bhānuḥ pradakṣiṇam avartata
english: Lomaśa said: "The sun used to go around in a clockwise direction — at rising and at setting — the great golden mountain Meru, that king of mountains."

sanskrit: taṃ tu dṛṣṭvā tathā vindhyaḥ śailaḥ sūryam athābravīt yathā hi merur bhavatā nityaśaḥ parigamyate pradakṣiṇaṃ ca kriyate mām evaṃ kuru bhāskara
english: "Seeing this, the Vindhya mountain then spoke to the sun: 'Just as Meru is constantly circumambulated by you in a clockwise manner, do the same for me, O maker of light.'"

sanskrit: evam uktas tataḥ sūryaḥ śailendraṃ pratyabhāṣata nāham ātmecchayā śaila karomy enaṃ pradakṣiṇam eṣa mārgaḥ pradiṣṭo me yenedaṃ nirmitaṃ jagat
english: "Thus addressed, the sun then replied to the lord of mountains: 'I do not circumambulate Meru of my own will, O mountain — this is the path prescribed for me by the one who created this world.'"

sanskrit: evam uktas tataḥ krodhāt pravṛddhaḥ sahasācalaḥ sūryācandramasor mārgaṃ roddhum icchan paraṃtapa
english: "Thus addressed, the mountain then suddenly began to swell up in anger, O chastiser of foes, wishing to block the path of the sun and moon."

sanskrit: tato devāḥ sahitāḥ sarva eva; sendrāḥ samāgamya mahādrirājam nivārayām āsur upāyatas taṃ; na ca sma teṣāṃ vacanaṃ cakāra
english: "Then all the gods together — along with Indra — came and tried by every means to restrain that great king of mountains; but he heeded not their words at all."

sanskrit: athābhijagmur munim āśramasthaṃ; tapasvinaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ variṣṭham agastyam atyadbhutavīryadīptaṃ; taṃ cārtham ūcuḥ sahitāḥ surās te
english: "Then the gods together went to the sage dwelling in his hermitage — to Agastya, the greatest bearer of dharma among the righteous, blazing with most wondrous power — and told him their purpose."

sanskrit: devā ūcuḥ sūryācandramasor mārgaṃ nakṣatrāṇāṃ gatiṃ tathā śailarājo vṛṇoty eṣa vindhyaḥ krodhavaśānugaḥ
english: The gods said: "This Vindhya, king of mountains, overcome by anger, is blocking the path of the sun and moon and likewise the course of the constellations."

sanskrit: taṃ nivārayituṃ śakto nānyaḥ kaś cid dvijottama ṛte tvāṃ hi mahābhāga tasmād enaṃ nivāraya
english: "No one else is capable of restraining him, O best of twice-born men, save you alone, O greatly blessed one. Therefore restrain him."

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca tac chrutvā vacanaṃ vipraḥ surāṇāṃ śailam abhyagāt so 'bhigamyābravīd vindhyaṃ sadāraḥ samupasthitaḥ
english: Lomaśa said: "Hearing those words of the gods, the brahmin went to the mountain; approaching Vindhya, together with his wife he addressed him as he stood before him."

sanskrit: mārgam icchāmy ahaṃ dattaṃ bhavatā parvatottama dakṣiṇām abhigantāsmi diśaṃ kāryeṇa kena cit
english: "'I desire passage granted by you, O best of mountains — I am going to the southern region for some purpose.'"

sanskrit: yāvadāgamanaṃ mahyaṃ tāvat tvaṃ pratipālaya nivṛtte mayi śailendra tato vardhasva kāmataḥ
english: "'Until my return, wait for me; when I have come back, O lord of mountains, then grow as you please.'"

sanskrit: evaṃ sa samayaṃ kṛtvā vindhyenāmitrakarśana adyāpi dakṣiṇād deśād vāruṇir na nivartate
english: "Having made this agreement with Vindhya, O crusher of foes, Agastya, the son of Varuṇa, has not returned from the southern land even to this day."

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ yathā vindhyo na vardhate agastyasya prabhāvena yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi
english: "All this has now been told to you — how the Vindhya does not grow, by the power of Agastya — which you asked me about."

sanskrit: kāleyās tu yathā rājan suraiḥ sarvair niṣūditāḥ agastyād varam āsādya tan me nigadataḥ śṛṇu
english: "Now hear from me as I tell how the Kāleyas were slain by all the gods, O king, after a boon was obtained from Agastya."

sanskrit: tridaśānāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā maitrāvaruṇir abravīt kimartham abhiyātāḥ stha varaṃ mattaḥ kim icchatha evam uktās tatas tena devās taṃ munim abruvan
english: "Hearing the words of the gods, Agastya, son of Mitra and Varuṇa, said: 'Why have you come to me? What boon do you seek from me?' Thus addressed by him, the gods then spoke to the sage."

sanskrit: evaṃ tvayecchāma kṛtaṃ maharṣe; mahārṇavaṃ pīyamānaṃ mahātman tato vadhiṣyāma sahānubandhān; kāleyasaṃjñān suravidviṣas tān
english: "'We wish this to be done by you, O great sage, O great-souled one: drink up the great ocean; then we shall slay those enemies of the gods known as the Kāleyas, together with all their followers.'"

sanskrit: tridaśānāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā tatheti munir abravīt kariṣye bhavatāṃ kāmaṃ lokānāṃ ca mahat sukham
english: "Hearing the words of the gods, the sage replied, 'So be it' — 'I shall fulfil your wish and bring great happiness to the worlds.'"

sanskrit: evam uktvā tato 'gacchat samudraṃ saritāṃ patim ṛṣibhiś ca tapaḥsiddhaiḥ sārdhaṃ devaiś ca suvrataḥ
english: Having spoken thus, that sage of excellent vows then went to the ocean, the lord of rivers, accompanied by sages perfected through austerity and by the gods.

sanskrit: manuṣyoragagandharvayakṣakiṃpuruṣās tathā anujagmur mahātmānaṃ draṣṭukāmās tad adbhutam
english: Humans, serpents, gandharvas, yakṣas, and kiṃpuruṣas likewise followed that great-souled one, eager to witness that wonder.

sanskrit: tato 'bhyagacchan sahitāḥ samudraṃ bhīmanisvanam nṛtyantam iva cormībhir valgantam iva vāyunā
english: They then all drew near together to the ocean with its terrifying roar, which seemed to dance with its waves and to leap about like the wind.

sanskrit: hasantam iva phenaughaiḥ skhalantaṃ kandareṣu ca nānāgrāhasamākīrṇaṃ nānādvijagaṇāyutam
english: Seeming to laugh with its surging foam, stumbling into its caverns, teeming with all manner of sea-monsters, and filled with countless flocks of birds of every kind.

sanskrit: agastyasahitā devāḥ sagandharvamahoragāḥ ṛṣayaś ca mahābhāgāḥ samāsedur mahodadhim
english: The gods together with Agastya, along with gandharvas and great serpents, and the greatly blessed sages, approached the vast deep.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca samudraṃ sa samāsādya vāruṇir bhagavān ṛṣiḥ uvāca sahitān devān ṛṣīṃś caiva samāgatān
english: Lomaśa said: "Having arrived at the ocean, the blessed sage, son of Varuṇa, spoke to the assembled gods and sages who had gathered together."

sanskrit: eṣa lokahitārthaṃ vai pibāmi varuṇālayam bhavadbhir yad anuṣṭheyaṃ tac chīghraṃ saṃvidhīyatām
english: "'For the welfare of the world, I shall now drink up this abode of Varuṇa. Let that which needs to be done by you all be arranged swiftly.'"

sanskrit: etāvad uktvā vacanaṃ maitrāvaruṇir acyutaḥ samudram apibat kruddhaḥ sarvalokasya paśyataḥ
english: Having said just these words, the steadfast son of Mitra and Varuṇa, filled with fierce resolve, drank up the ocean before the eyes of the entire world.

sanskrit: pīyamānaṃ samudraṃ tu dṛṣṭvā devāḥ savāsavāḥ vismayaṃ paramaṃ jagmuḥ stutibhiś cāpy apūjayan
english: Seeing the ocean being drunk up, the gods together with Vāsava were struck with supreme wonder, and they honored him with hymns of praise.

sanskrit: tvaṃ nas trātā vidhātā ca lokānāṃ lokabhāvanaḥ tvatprasādāt samucchedaṃ na gacchet sāmaraṃ jagat
english: "'You are our savior, the ordainer of the worlds, the nourisher of the worlds; by your grace, the world together with the gods will not come to utter destruction.'"

sanskrit: saṃpūjyamānas tridaśair mahātmā; gandharvatūryeṣu nadatsu sarvaśaḥ divyaiś ca puṣpair avakīryamāṇo; mahārṇavaṃ niḥsalilaṃ cakāra
english: Worshipped by the gods on all sides while gandharva music resounded everywhere, and showered with divine flowers, the great-souled one rendered the mighty ocean waterless.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā kṛtaṃ niḥsalilaṃ mahārṇavaṃ; surāḥ samastāḥ paramaprahṛṣṭāḥ pragṛhya divyāni varāyudhāni; tān dānavāñ jaghnur adīnasattvāḥ
english: Seeing the mighty ocean rendered waterless, all the gods were supremely joyful; taking up their divine and excellent weapons, those undaunted beings slew those demons.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānās tridaśair mahātmabhir; mahābalair vegibhir unnadadbhiḥ na sehire vegavatāṃ mahātmanāṃ; vegaṃ tadā dhārayituṃ divaukasām
english: Struck down by those great-souled gods of mighty power who charged forth with battle-cries, the demons could not at that time withstand the onslaught of those swift and great-souled dwellers of heaven.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānās tridaśair dānavā bhīmanisvanāḥ cakruḥ sutumulaṃ yuddhaṃ muhūrtam iva bhārata
english: Those terrible-roaring demons, being slain by the gods, fought a most tumultuous battle for a brief while, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: te pūrvaṃ tapasā dagdhā munibhir bhāvitātmabhiḥ yatamānāḥ paraṃ śaktyā tridaśair viniṣūditāḥ
english: Already scorched in former times by the austerities of the self-perfected sages, and now exerting their utmost strength, they were annihilated by the gods.

sanskrit: te hemaniṣkābharaṇāḥ kuṇḍalāṅgadadhāriṇaḥ nihatya bahv aśobhanta puṣpitā iva kiṃśukāḥ
english: Those slain demons, adorned with golden necklaces and wearing ear-rings and armlets, lay in great splendor like kiṃśuka trees in full bloom.

sanskrit: hataśeṣās tataḥ ke cit kāleyā manujottama vidārya vasudhāṃ devīṃ pātālatalam āśritāḥ
english: Then some of the surviving Kāleyas, O best of men, split open the earth goddess and took refuge in the depths of Pātāla.

sanskrit: nihatān dānavān dṛṣṭvā tridaśā munipuṃgavam tuṣṭuvur vividhair vākyair idaṃ caivābruvan vacaḥ
english: Seeing the demons slain, the gods praised the foremost of sages with various words and also spoke these words to him.

sanskrit: tvatprasādān mahābhāga lokaiḥ prāptaṃ mahat sukham tvattejasā ca nihatāḥ kāleyāḥ krūravikramāḥ
english: "'By your grace, O greatly blessed one, the worlds have attained great happiness; and by your power the Kāleyas of cruel valor have been slain.'"

sanskrit: pūrayasva mahābāho samudraṃ lokabhāvana yat tvayā salilaṃ pītaṃ tad asmin punar utsṛja
english: "'Fill the ocean again, O mighty-armed nourisher of the worlds; release back into it the water that you have drunk.'"

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ pratyuvāca bhagavān munipuṃgavaḥ jīrṇaṃ tad dhi mayā toyam upāyo 'nyaḥ pracintyatām pūraṇārthaṃ samudrasya bhavadbhir yatnam āsthitaiḥ
english: Thus addressed, the blessed foremost of sages replied: 'That water has indeed been digested by me. Some other means must be devised by you, striving with effort for the purpose of filling the ocean.'

sanskrit: etac chrutvā tu vacanaṃ maharṣer bhāvitātmanaḥ vismitāś ca viṣaṇṇāś ca babhūvuḥ sahitāḥ surāḥ
english: Having heard this word of the great sage of perfected soul, all the gods together were filled with amazement and became downcast.

sanskrit: parasparam anujñāpya praṇamya munipuṃgavam prajāḥ sarvā mahārāja viprajagmur yathāgatam
english: Taking leave of one another and bowing to that foremost of sages, O great king, all creatures departed the way they had come.

sanskrit: tridaśā viṣṇunā sārdham upajagmuḥ pitāmaham pūraṇārthaṃ samudrasya mantrayitvā punaḥ punaḥ ūcuḥ prāñjalayaḥ sarve sāgarasyābhipūraṇam
english: The gods, together with Viṣṇu, went to the Grandsire and, having deliberated again and again about the filling of the ocean, all spoke with joined palms concerning the replenishment of the sea.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca tān uvāca sametāṃs tu brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ gacchadhvaṃ vibudhāḥ sarve yathākāmaṃ yathepsitam
english: Lomaśa said: "To those assembled gods, Brahmā, the Grandsire of the worlds, spoke: 'Go, O gods, all of you, as you desire and as you wish.'"

sanskrit: mahatā kālayogena prakṛtiṃ yāsyate 'rṇavaḥ jñātīn vai kāraṇaṃ kṛtvā mahārājño bhagīrathāt
english: "'In the fullness of great time the ocean will return to its natural state, making the kinsmen of the great king Bhagīratha the cause thereof.'"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kathaṃ vai jñātayo brahman kāraṇaṃ cātra kiṃ mune kathaṃ samudraḥ pūrṇaś ca bhagīrathapariśramāt
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "How are his kinsmen the cause, O brahmin? What is that cause, O sage? And how was the ocean filled through the exertions of Bhagīratha?"
